## Oral Microbiology Research

**Lewin Lab | Case Western Reserve University | May 2026–Present**

I study interactions between oral streptococci and *Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans* (*Aa*), a bacterium associated with periodontal disease. My work involves using reflectometric assays to measure hydrogen peroxide and L-lactate production across oral streptococcal strains.

Through this research, I have gained experience culturing bacteria, preparing media, measuring metabolites, and communicating findings through poster presentations.

### Pathology Retreat | Fall 2026

**Quantifying Differences in Hydrogen Peroxide and L-lactate Production across Oral Streptococci using an Optimized Reflectometric Assay**

This presentation explores differences in metabolite production across oral streptococci and how these differences may help us understand bacterial interactions in periodontal disease.

### Summer Intersections | 2026

**Quantifying Differences in Hydrogen Peroxide and L-lactate Production across Oral Streptococci using an Optimized Reflectometric Assay**

At Summer Intersections, I presented my work using an optimized reflectometric assay to compare hydrogen peroxide and L-lactate production across oral streptococci. The poster includes the project background, abstract, methods, and findings.

## DNA Phase Separation Research

**Ngo Lab | OHSU Knight Cancer Institute, CEDAR | Summer 2025**

### Polyamine-Induced DNA Phase Separation Length Dependence

During my research internship at Oregon Health & Science University, I investigated how DNA fragment length influences polyamine-induced phase separation. My work included preparing DNA fragments, PCR, gel electrophoresis, and phase separation assays.

I presented this project at the OHSU symposium.

[View poster](ohsu-2025-poster.pdf){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}
